'''''Escargots à la bourguignonne''''' is a French dish of snails with garlic butter.

==Ingredients==
* 24 canned [[Cookbook:Snail|snails]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]] [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] or minced [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1½ tbsp fresh [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Pepper]], to taste
* 24 snail shells, with snail serving dishes, and snail tongs OR 4 glazed indented earthenware snail serving dishes OR 24 small [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushroom]] caps, trimmed and de-gilled
==Procedure==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 400°F.
# Drain and rinse the snails.
# Combine the butter with the shallots, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper, and blend well.
# [[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] the mushroom caps, if using, in a small amount of garlic butter until cooked but still firm. Remove from the heat.
# If using snail shells, place a snail in each shell and fill the rest of the space with garlic butter. If using a snail dish without the shells, place a snail in each indentation and fill the rest of the space with garlic butter. If using mushroom caps, place 2–3 snails in each cap and top with a generous amount of garlic butter.
# Heat the snails in the oven for 5–7 minutes, and serve with copious quantities of French [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] for soaking up the garlic butter.
